Subject: High 502/error rate + token latency impacting ingest (EastUS) - urgent

Michael —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 502s and per-token latency for our ingestion route (POST /v1/ingest) around 06:00 PDT this morning. Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~18% and p95 latency went from ~220ms to >2.4s. Traffic for Emerald's production fleet is concentrated in EastUS (us-east-1 equivalent). Our retry logic is causing downstream bursts and some requests are timing out.

Logs show repeated 502s with short-lived connection resets; sample request-ids attached. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an infrastructure/regional outage or a model-serving degradation? This is impacting our SLAs — customers are seeing ingestion failures.

We need an ETA for stabilization or a plan to route traffic to a fallback region. Please treat as high priority and loop in execs if needed.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Ops Lead, Emerald Energy

Infra — passing along samples from Emerald and our initial trace analysis. Key observations: 
- KV cache eviction pattern shows unusually high churn starting 05:50 PDT; correlates to the routing microchange rolled out earlier this morning.
- Model-serving worker processes show transient OOMs on several hosts; restart loops triggered autoscaler but warm-up lag created request backpressure.
- Some front door LB sockets are returning 502s due to upstream resets; unclear whether this is a network fabric blip or process-level crash.

Immediate asks: 
- Snapshot and preserve /var/log/serving for 05:30–09:00 (we attached svclogs).
- Consider rolling back the routing microchange for the ingest route (rev-20270615-0457).
- If rollback not possible fast enough, prepare failover play to US-West.
